INVESTMENT POLICY OF THE EXAMPLE REGIONAL WATER AUTHORITY

I. ADOPTION
This written investment policy was adopted by resolution of the Board of Directors
on October 1, 2025, with an effective date of October 1, 2025.

II. OBJECTIVES AND STANDARD OF CARE
The primary objectives, in order of priority, are preservation and safety of principal,
liquidity, and yield. Yield is subordinate to safety of principal and liquidity.
Investments shall be made with judgment and care, under prevailing circumstances, that a
person of prudence, discretion, and intelligence would exercise in the management of the
person's own affairs, not for speculation, but for investment. In determining whether the
Investment Officer has exercised prudence, the determination is made across all funds
under the Officer's responsibility rather than a consideration as to the prudence of a
single investment, and by reference to whether the decision was consistent with the
written investment policy of the Authority.

III. INVESTMENT MANAGEMENT
This policy addresses investment diversification, yield, and maturity, and the quality
and capability of investment management, including officer designation, qualifications,
and training.

IV. INVESTMENT STRATEGIES
A separate investment strategy is adopted for each fund group. For the operating fund,
the debt service fund, and the capital project fund, each strategy addresses suitability,
preservation and safety of principal, liquidity, marketability, diversification of the
investment portfolio, and yield, in that order of importance.

V. AUTHORIZED INVESTMENTS
The following investments are authorized, and investments not listed are not authorized
notwithstanding any authority conferred by Chapter 2256: obligations of the United States
and its agencies, certificates of deposit, fully collateralized repurchase agreements, and
eligible investment pools. Commercial paper is authorized with a stated maturity of 270
days or fewer, rated by at least one nationally recognized credit rating agency.
Bids for certificates of deposit may be solicited orally, in writing, electronically, or
in any combination of those methods.

Government obligations are limited to obligations of the United States or its agencies
and instrumentalities, direct obligations of this state or its agencies, and obligations
unconditionally guaranteed or insured by, or backed by the full faith and credit of, this
state or the United States. Collateralized mortgage obligations are limited to those
directly issued by a federal agency or instrumentality the underlying security for which
is federally guaranteed. Interest-only strips, principal-only strips, collateralized
mortgage obligations with a stated final maturity greater than ten years, and inverse
floating rate collateralized mortgage obligations are not authorized.

Certificates of deposit must be issued by a depository institution that has its main
office or a branch office in this state and must be guaranteed or insured by the Federal
Deposit Insurance Corporation or the National Credit Union Share Insurance Fund, or
secured by obligations described by Section 2256.009(a) having a market value of not less
than the principal amount of the certificates, excluding those described by Section
2256.009(b), or secured in accordance with Chapter 2257.

Each authorized investment pool must be continuously rated no lower than AAA or AAA-m or
at an equivalent rating by at least one nationally recognized rating service, and the
Board authorizes investment in each particular pool by resolution after review of the
pool's offering circular. The pool must furnish transaction confirmations and a monthly
report.

VI. MATURITY LIMITS
The maximum stated maturity of any individual investment is 24 months for the operating
fund and 60 months for the debt service fund. For pooled fund groups, the maximum
dollar-weighted average maturity allowed, based on the stated maturity date for the
portfolio, is 270 days.

VII. MARKET PRICE MONITORING
The market value of all investments is determined monthly using an independent pricing
source retained by the Authority and independent of any counterparty to the transaction.

VIII. SETTLEMENT
All securities transactions, other than investment pool funds and mutual funds, shall be
settled on a delivery versus payment basis.

IX. RATING MONITORING AND LOSS OF RATING
The Investment Officer shall monitor rating changes in all investments acquired with
public funds on a monthly basis. An investment that requires a minimum rating does not
qualify as an authorized investment during the period the investment does not have the
minimum rating, and the Authority shall take all prudent measures consistent with this
policy to liquidate any such investment.

X. INVESTMENT OFFICER
The Board of Directors designates by resolution one or more officers or employees of the
Authority as Investment Officer, responsible for the investment of its funds consistent
with this policy. Authority granted is effective until rescinded, until the expiration of
the officer's term, or until termination of employment. The Investment Officer shall
exercise the judgment and care a prudent person would exercise in the management of the
person's own affairs. The Board of Directors retains ultimate responsibility as fiduciary
of the assets of the Authority.

XI. BROKER LIST
The Board of Directors shall at least annually review, revise, and adopt a list of
qualified brokers authorized to engage in investment transactions with the Authority.

XII. BUSINESS ORGANIZATIONS
A written copy of the investment policy shall be presented to any business organization
offering to engage in an investment transaction. A qualified representative shall execute
a written instrument certifying that it has received and reviewed the investment policy
and implemented reasonable procedures and controls. The Investment Officer may not acquire
any authorized investment from a business organization that has not delivered the
instrument required by Subsection (k).

XIII. ANNUAL REVIEW
The Board of Directors shall review this investment policy and the investment strategies
not less than annually and shall adopt a written instrument stating that it has reviewed
the investment policy and investment strategies and shall record any changes.

XIV. REPORTING AND AUDIT
Not less than quarterly the Investment Officer shall prepare a written report of
investment transactions for all funds, signed by each investment officer, presented to the
governing body and the chief executive officer. The report states the beginning market
value, ending market value, and fully accrued interest for each pooled fund group, the
book value and market value of each separately invested asset, the maturity date of each
such asset, the fund for which it was acquired, and compliance with the investment
strategy and with the relevant provisions of Chapter 2256. The investment reports shall be
formally reviewed at least annually by an independent auditor, and the result of the
review shall be reported to the governing body. A compliance audit of management controls
on investments and adherence to this policy is performed in conjunction with the annual
financial audit.
